CyberDefendersNetwork ForensicsMediumWireshark · NetworkMiner · Brim
Scenario: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in the organization's JetBrains TeamCity server, uploaded a webshell, and took full control of the host — then used it as a launch point for further activity, including data manipulation. Working purely from a packet capture, the task is to reconstruct the timeline: the entry point, the attacker's tooling, and the extent of the compromise.
CVE-2024-27198 is an authentication bypass in TeamCity's web component: a protected REST request carrying a crafted ;.jsp suffix is treated as a request for a page that needs no login. In this capture it appears as GET /hax?jsp=/app/rest/server;.jsp returning 200 with no credentials. The rest of the chain is just as visible in cleartext HTTP on port 8111: create a SYSTEM_ADMIN user through the REST API, mint an API token, upload a malicious plugin ZIP via /admin/pluginUpload.html, then drive the JSP webshell inside it with cmd= POST requests. Follow → HTTP Stream is enough to read every step.
Q1Identifying the attacker's IP address helps trace the source and stop further attacks. What is the attacker's IP address?
Statistics → Conversations → IPv4 puts 23.158.56.196 at the top, with 4,166 packets (~1 MB) to 172.17.0.2 and 2,083 packets (~1 MB) to 172.31.25.119. The same sessions appearing under two internal addresses is consistent with the capture seeing both sides of Docker's NAT — 172.17.0.0/16 is Docker's default bridge range — which foreshadows the container escape in Q9.
answer23.158.56.196
Q2To identify potential vulnerability exploitation, what version of our web server service is running?
Right-click the GET /hax?jsp=/app/rest/server;.jsp request → Follow → HTTP Stream. TeamCity's REST API answers with XML that reports version="2023.11.3 (build 147512)", served to an unauthenticated client.
answer2023.11.3
Q3After identifying the version of our web server service, what CVE number corresponds to the vulnerability the attacker exploited?
NVD describes it as an authentication bypass in TeamCity before 2023.11.4 that allows admin actions — CVSS 3.1 base score 9.8 Critical (network, low complexity, no privileges, no user interaction). Version 2023.11.3 is one patch release short of the fix.
answerCVE-2024-27198
Q4What credentials did the attacker successfully use for Basic Auth against the TeamCity server?
http.request.method == GET and ip.addr == 23.158.56.196
The attacker's GET list shows repeated hits on /authenticationTest.html?csrf (TeamCity's credential-check endpoint) next to the ;.jsp bypass requests. Following the stream of the bypass reveals the account being provisioned: a JSON body creating user c91oyemw with role SYSTEM_ADMIN, and a 200 response echoing the new user (id 2).
answerc91oyemw:CL5vzdwLuK
Q5The attacker uploaded a webshell to ensure his access to the system. What is the name of the file that the attacker uploaded?
http.request.method == POST and ip.addr == 23.158.56.196
Among the POSTs, a multipart request to /admin/pluginUpload.html carries filename="NSt8bHTg.zip" with an Authorization: Bearer … header. A TeamCity plugin is just a ZIP; the stream shows it packs server/NSt8bHTg.jar plus buildServerResources/NSt8bHTg.jsp, a page that reads a cmd request parameter — the webshell itself. Later commands go to /plugins/NSt8bHTg/NSt8bHTg.jsp.
answerNSt8bHTg.zip
Q6When did the attacker execute their first command via the web shell?
frame contains "cmd" and ip.addr == 23.158.56.196
The first webshell request is frame 25572: a POST to /plugins/NSt8bHTg/NSt8bHTg.jsp at 2024-06-30 08:03:57 (consistent with the GMT Date headers in the surrounding responses). Wireshark's HTML Form URL Encoded pane shows cmd=ls — a directory listing, the classic first move on a new shell.
answer2024-06-30 08:03
Q7The attacker tampered with a text file that contained the credentials of the admin user of the webserver. What new username and password did the attacker write in the file?
http.request.method == POST and ip.addr == 23.158.56.196
One webshell POST carries cmd=bash -c 'echo "username:a1l4m,password:youarecompromised" > /tmp/Creds.txt'. The single > overwrites the file, replacing the stored admin credentials with attacker-chosen values. Answer format: username:password, no labels.
answera1l4m:youarecompromised
Q8Q7 showed the attacker writing false credentials into Creds.txt. Which MITRE ATT&CK sub-technique (Data Manipulation family) describes that specific file-write action?
T1565.001 — Stored Data Manipulation (Impact tactic): altering data at rest to compromise its integrity — here, a credentials file on the host. Its siblings are T1565.002 (Transmitted) and T1565.003 (Runtime Data Manipulation).
answerT1565.001
Q9Immediately after gaining a shell, the attacker executed a docker command that mounted the host filesystem and chrooted into it — providing full host access. What was that exact command? (Do NOT include the cmd= prefix seen in the HTTP body.)
ip.addr == 23.158.56.196 and http.request.method == POST and frame contains "cmd="
-v /:/host mounts the host's entire root filesystem into a throwaway Ubuntu container (--rm), and chroot /host makes that mount the shell's root — effectively root on the underlying host, escaping the TeamCity container. It only works because the TeamCity process could reach the Docker daemon.
answerdocker run --rm -it -v /:/host ubuntu chroot /host

Lessons learned: Patch to 2023.11.4 or later — and keep CI/CD servers off the public internet, since a single unauthenticated /app/rest/server request also fingerprints the exact version for the attacker. The chain leaves alertable HTTP indicators at every step: ;.jsp suffixes or ?jsp= on /app/rest paths, a POST creating a SYSTEM_ADMIN user, token creation, pluginUpload.html from an unknown IP, then POSTs with cmd= to a plugin's JSP. Port 8111 ran plain HTTP, which is why the whole attack was readable — terminate TLS in front of it. Finally, a build server whose process can reach the Docker daemon is one command from host root; avoid mounting the Docker socket into it. (Rapid7 also disclosed a sibling flaw, CVE-2024-27199, a path-traversal issue fixed in the same release.)
